rubric_items.reason: Covers authorisation, validation, injection, data exposure, error leakage and the N+1 cost. It misses that ids above the int4 maximum pass parseId and end in a 500. It also does not triage the four SAST results.
SF-1 cites the exact loop line (L184). Most claims cite the exact lines. C4 cites L21-L22, but its 'up to ten digits' detail comes from the regex on L18.
SF-1 is rated minor. That fits an authenticated, read-only, unpaged route whose cost grows with doctor count. No severity looks inflated or understated.
The fix direction for SF-1 is concrete: batch the availability and occupyingBetween reads into one query each.
No false positives. The one finding is real: the per-doctor queries in the loop at doctorService.ts L184-L187 exist.

findings.text: parseId accepts ids up to 9999999999, but specialization.id is a serial (int4) column. An id such as 3000000000 reaches refStatus, Postgres raises out-of-range, and the route answers 500 instead of 404. The review says malformed ids are fully handled.

cites.quote: res.status(500).json({ error: { code: 'INTERNAL', message: 'Something went wrong' } });
the malformed id is rejected by `parseId`

findings.suggested_fix: Add a minor finding: ids above 2147483647 give a 500. The fix direction is for parseId (or this route) to reject ids above the int4 maximum with a 400. Note that this behaviour predates the change.
